paragraphs.title: The Day of the Locusts and Terror

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Blow ye the trumpet in Zion.”
easy.q: What is the prophet commanded to blow in Zion?

answers: A day of darkness and gloominess
easy.explanation: The KJV calls it “a day of darkness and of gloominess.”
easy.q: How is the day of the LORD first described?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “The appearance of them is as the appearance of horses; and as horsemen, so shall they run.”
easy.q: What do the army’s appearance and movement resemble?

answers: A fire before it and a flame behind it
Rain before it and snow behind it
Wind before it and silence behind it
medium.explanation: A fire devours before them, and behind them a flame burns.
medium.q: What is before the army and what is behind it?

answers: Because the day of the LORD is near
Because the harvest will be plentiful
medium.explanation: The people are told to tremble because the day of the LORD “cometh” and “is nigh at hand.”
medium.q: Why will the inhabitants of the land tremble?

medium.explanation: The expression describes the terror and anguish appearing on the people’s faces.
medium.q: In the sentence “all faces shall gather blackness,” what does “blackness” convey?

answers: It is like the garden of Eden before them and a desolate wilderness behind them
It is a wilderness before them and a garden of Eden behind them
It is a sea before them and mountains behind them
challenge.explanation: The land is described as Eden before the army and a desolate wilderness behind it.
challenge.q: What contrast describes the army’s effect on the land?

answers: Each one follows his own path without breaking ranks
The army stops before the wall
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that each one proceeds in his path and does not break ranks or thrust another.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the statement that they “shall march every one on his ways”?

answers: From the city to the countryside only
From the land to the heavens only
From the land and city to the sun, moon, and stars
challenge.explanation: The earth and city are affected first, and then the heavens, sun, moon, and stars are described as trembling or darkened.
challenge.q: How does the description of terror expand?

paragraphs.title: A Call to Repentance and Prayer

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “turn ye even to me with all your heart.”
easy.q: To whom does the LORD call the people to return?

easy.explanation: The passage calls for fasting, weeping, and mourning.
easy.q: With what actions are the people called to return?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Let the priests, the ministers of the LORD, weep between the porch and the altar.”
easy.q: Who is told to weep between the porch and the altar?

answers: Repentance should be inward and genuine
medium.explanation: The command points to a sincere change of heart rather than merely an outward action.
medium.q: What does “rend your heart, and not your garments” emphasize?

answers: To hold a solemn assembly and pray together
medium.explanation: The people, congregation, elders, children, nursing infants, bridegroom, and bride are all called to assemble.
medium.q: Why are all the people commanded to gather?

medium.explanation: A solemn assembly is a public gathering called for a serious religious purpose.
medium.q: What does “solemn assembly” mean in this passage?

answers: So the heathen will rule over the land
So the heathen will not ask, “Where is their God?”
So the people will leave the land
challenge.explanation: The priests fear that the nations will mock Israel by asking where its God is.
challenge.q: Why do the priests ask the LORD not to give his heritage to reproach?

answers: It includes every part of the community
challenge.explanation: The list includes people of every age and circumstance, showing that the gathering is for the whole community.
challenge.q: What does the mention of infants, bridegroom, and bride show about the assembly?

answers: Because he is gracious and merciful, there is hope in returning to him
He does not listen to the people
He wants the people to fight
challenge.explanation: The LORD is described as gracious, merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, giving the people reason to repent.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between the LORD’s character and the call to repentance?

paragraphs.title: Divine Compassion and the Removal of the Locusts

easy.explanation: The verse says that the LORD will “pity his people.”
easy.q: Upon whom does the LORD have pity?

easy.explanation: The LORD promises, “I will send you corn, and wine, and oil.”
easy.q: What does the LORD promise to send to his people?

answers: Into a land barren and desolate
easy.explanation: The LORD says he will drive the northern army into “a land barren and desolate.”
easy.q: Where will the northern army be driven?

answers: The people will be satisfied with them
The people will give them to the heathen
medium.explanation: The LORD says, “ye shall be satisfied therewith.”
medium.q: What will be the result of receiving the corn, wine, and oil?

answers: The source of the threat will be removed
The people will leave the land
medium.explanation: The LORD promises to remove the northern army far away from his people.
medium.q: What does the removal of the northern army show about the situation?

medium.explanation: “Barren” describes land that is dry, empty, and unable to produce crops.
medium.q: What does “barren” mean in the phrase “a land barren and desolate”?

answers: Both express his care for the land and the people
Both express his desire to destroy everything
They have no connection in the passage
challenge.explanation: The verse joins the LORD’s concern for his land with his compassion for his people.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between the LORD’s jealousy for his land and his pity for his people?

answers: It is presented as a disgusting and harmful plague
It is presented as a source of blessing
challenge.explanation: Its “stink” and “ill savour” emphasize the unpleasantness and seriousness of the plague.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the description of the army’s smell after it is removed?

answers: The plague had destroyed the land’s agricultural abundance
The people did not practice farming
These products are unrelated to the land
challenge.explanation: Restoring these crops directly answers the destruction caused by the locust army.
challenge.q: Why is the promise of corn, wine, and oil especially meaningful after the locust plague?

paragraphs.title: Restoration and Abundance After the Plague

easy.explanation: The verse speaks directly to the land and tells it not to fear.
easy.q: To whom is the command “Fear not, O land” addressed?

answers: They will be full and overflowing
easy.explanation: The floors will be full of wheat, and the vats will overflow with wine and oil.
easy.q: What will happen to the floors and vats?

answers: That the LORD is in the midst of Israel
That the locusts are stronger than the LORD
That the heathen rule the land
easy.explanation: The people will know that the LORD is in the midst of Israel and is their God.
easy.q: What will the people know after the restoration?

answers: Because the rains will return and the land will flourish
Because the people will leave the land
medium.explanation: The passage speaks of rain, fruitfulness, and renewed agricultural abundance.
medium.q: Why are the children of Zion told to be glad and rejoice?

answers: Rain, growth, full floors and vats, and praise
medium.explanation: The verses describe restoration leading to satisfaction and praise of the LORD.
medium.q: What sequence is described after the plague?

medium.explanation: The former rain is the early rain, distinguished from the latter rain mentioned in the verse.
medium.q: What does “former rain” mean in this passage?

answers: The land changes from devastated and desolate to fertile and abundant
The land changes from peaceful to abandoned
The land changes from fertile to completely dry
challenge.explanation: The locusts devastate the land, but the LORD later restores its fruitfulness and abundance.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the beginning of the chapter and the restoration passages?

answers: The LORD will restore what was lost during the years of the plague
The LORD will lengthen the years of the plague
The LORD will abolish the seasons
challenge.explanation: The promise refers to restoring what was consumed by the locusts and other destroying insects.
challenge.q: What does the promise “I will restore to you the years” mean?

answers: The abundance leads the people to praise the LORD and know that he is among them
The abundance causes the people to ignore the LORD
The abundance proves that the locusts are divine
challenge.explanation: After eating and being satisfied, the people praise the LORD and know that he is in their midst.
challenge.q: How is agricultural abundance connected with knowing the LORD?
